chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Razzaz Al-Qurashi narrated to me, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee', from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Yahya ibn Ma'mar al-Attar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Mankind, Jinn, birds, and beasts wept over al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) until their tears flowed profusely.

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, all of them, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, through his chain, similarly.
ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the reaction of all creation to the martyrdom of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* illustrates the cosmic scale of Imam al-Husayn’s martyrdom, where the weeping of humans, jinn, birds, and beasts signifies a universal mourning that transcends earthly boundaries. The dual transmission chains underscore the authenticity and widespread acceptance of this event within Shia scholarly tradition, reinforcing the concept of *al-Gharam* (the divine debt of love) owed by all creation to the Ahl al-Bayt. It serves as a theological foundation for the belief that the tragedy of Karbala was not merely a historical incident but a metaphysical event affecting the entire universe.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz Al-Qurashi narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’, from Abī Ismā’īl Al-Sarrāj, from Yaḥyā ibn Mu’ammar Al-‘Aťťār, from Abī Basīr, who said:
Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)) said: Mankind, Jinn, birds, and the beasts all shed tears and cried over (the killing of) Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.).

The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father and all of my scholars, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Abī Khalaf, and from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā Al-‘Aťťār, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Muḥamad ibn Ismā’īl, from Abī Ismā’īl Al-Sarrāj, from Yaḥyā ibn Mu’ammar Al-‘Aťťār, from Abī Basīr, from Abī Ja’far (a.s.).
